messages:
lina: FYI incoming from Helio Health — they flagged a $12.4k burst on their Dedicated commit for Feb and are asking for an SLA credit. invoice INV-2042 attached to the support ticket.
omar: Can you paste the invoice line? I don't have the PDF yet.
kevin-fin: Quick summary: customer has a 10k reserved commit. Failover to eu-west caused cross-region bursts from 02/14 03:10-03:46 UTC. Billing shows 98 GPU-hours billed as burst.
kevin-fin: invoice snippet:
```
INV-2042
- Reserved commit (Feb): $10,000
- Burst overage (eu-west failover 02/14): $12,400
- SLA credit applied? NO
Total due: $22,400
```

marta: Do we already have monitoring events showing the failover? SRE bot should have alert history.
sre-bot: Alert: dedicated-failover-us->eu at 2026-02-14T03:09:58Z. Autoscale fired, 6 nodes launched. Traffic shifted for 36 minutes. (link to runbook)
omar: OK. Two questions: 1) Is the burst legitimately billable per the TOS/commit rules? 2) If not, what's the credit calc? We need an ask for finance to send to AE.
kevin-fin: Per contract: commit covers steady-state capacity by region. Failover >15m that materially increases peak is chargeable unless it's a documented platform incident with SLA miss. Does this meet SLA miss criteria? We need p99 latency and availability windows.
lina: Helio claims they saw tail latency >2s during the period and lost some requests. They want a full burst refund + goodwill credit. They CC'd the AE.
marta: From infra telemetry: a subset of requests experienced degraded p99 for ~12 minutes; overall availability stayed above SLA. No automated rollback triggered. Hard call.
kevin-fin: Proposal: Offer a partial credit = pro-rated burst charge for the period where p99 > SLA threshold. That reduces $12.4k -> approx $4.5k. Plus one-month reserved bump discount as goodwill (10% off next month). Want approval to offer that to Helio.
omar: Need sign-off from finance lead + CS. pinging @marta and @kevin-fin: please confirm the calculation and the wording we'll send.
marta: Confirm calculation method. I ran the windowed p99 and estimate 37% of the burst is attributable to SLA degradation window. 37% * $12,400 = $4,588 -> round to $4,600 credit.
kevin-fin: I'll draft the credit memo. Text suggestion: "We reviewed the incident and are applying a $4,600 SLA credit to INV-2042 for the impacted interval, plus a 10% discount on your next month's reserved commit invoice as a goodwill gesture." Approve?
lina: Approve from AE side pending CS copy. @omar can you finalize invoice adjustment and issue a credit note?
omar: Will do. I'll create CN-2042-1 and apply $4,600. Also adding internal tag: reason=failover_partial-sla-credit. I'll update the billing ticket and notify the AE.
kevin-fin: Also flagging to Billing-bot to not auto-collect on INV-2042 until CN applied.
billing-bot: Action queued: hold collection on INV-2042 until credit note CN-2042-1 posted. (ETA 30m)
lina: Thanks all. I'll reply to Helio with the proposed credit and the next-steps timeline.
kevin-fin: Leaving a note for retrospective: check failover routing policies + failover accounting to avoid cross-region burst billing in similar partial-degradation cases. Might need a policy exception.
omar: Filed internal JIRA FIN-872: "Adjust failover billing policy / add handling for partial SLA outages". Assigning to kevin-fin and platform.
lina: Closing thread — will update when credit is live and Helio accepts. :white_check_mark:
